issues.claim: The documentation warns explicitly that the app may never resume from this state: the operating system may terminate the process to free memory, and no event is raised before that.
issues.problem: The MAUI doc only says there is 'no guarantee that an app will resume from this state, because it may be terminated by the operating system'. It does not say no event is raised. Its lifecycle text says that when a device terminates a stopped app 'the Destroying event is raised'. The claim that Destroying is not raised therefore conflicts with the cited MAUI page. It is true in practice for Android process kills, but it is not a doc quote.
issues.suggestedFix: Credit the MAUI doc only with the 'no guarantee the app resumes' warning. Credit the Android process-lifecycle page for 'the system can kill the process at any time to reclaim memory without running further app code'. Add that the MAUI doc describes Destroying as raised in this case, but in practice it cannot be relied on after a process kill. Reword the RU text the same way.
